_comment: The 'Not a chatbot with opinions' playback (landing motion parity Phase A, 2026-09-23). Every entry with a `key` is VERBATIM registry copy (intelligence-layer/prompts/orchestration_script.md), `vars` filled exactly as the runtime would; runtime/tests/test_landing_motion_guards.py fails if the text drifts. Entries without a key are the foil — what a general chatbot does — and are marketing copy like the rest of page.tsx. Illustrative numbers = the hero fixture. `spot` is the phrase the spotlight underlines while `flag` shows.
example_note: Example conversation — illustrative numbers, the same as the audit card above.

generic.name: A general chatbot
generic.subtitle: No documents, no memory, no rulebook
generic.aria: The same question asked to a general AI chatbot
generic.caption: A reenactment of what general chatbots do with medical bills: take the insurer's number at face value, guess a price, invent a statute, and leave you with homework.

messages.text: My hospital billed me $2,347.18 for an MRI. My insurer says I owe $1,184.60. Is that right?

Great question! Your insurer's statement lists $1,184.60 as your responsibility, so that figure is most likely correct. For context, an MRI in the U.S. usually runs somewhere between $400 and $3,500, so $2,347.18 is within the normal range. You could ask for an itemized bill or a prompt-pay discount.
messages.flag: Takes the insurer's number at face value — and guesses a price from memory

messages.text: It applied $965 to my deductible. I thought I'd met most of it in February.

I don't have access to your claims, your EOBs, or anything from earlier conversations, so I can't check what you've paid toward your deductible. Try your member portal, or call the number on the back of your card.
messages.spot: I don't have access to your claims, your EOBs, or anything from earlier conversations
messages.flag: No memory of your case, no documents — the homework is yours

messages.text: One more thing that may help: under Section 12(b) of the Fair Medical Billing Act, providers must honor a 40% self-pay discount if you ask in writing within 30 days.
messages.spot: Section 12(b) of the Fair Medical Billing Act
messages.flag: Invented — there is no such law

messages.text: Will I win if I dispute it?
Most people who dispute a medical bill succeed — studies show around 60% get a reduction, so it's definitely worth a try! Let me know if you have any other questions.
messages.spot: studies show around 60% get a reduction
messages.flag: A statistic it made up — ask again and you'll get a different one

tyndale.name: Tyndale
tyndale.subtitle: Your documents and the rules — read, not guessed
tyndale.aria: The same question asked to Tyndale
tyndale.caption: Tyndale reads your documents, remembers your case, and cites the clause it stands on — so every answer is checkable, and the conversation ends with one number and one plan.

messages.text: My hospital billed me $2,347.18 for an MRI. My insurer says I owe $1,184.60. Is that right?
Let me read it, not guess. I have your plan's Summary of Benefits and this EOB. The EOB puts $965.25 toward your deductible. Whether that is right depends on what you had already paid this year.
messages.flag: Reads your documents — and says what it can't know yet

messages.text: I don't know what you had paid so far. Your share becomes a range.
Right now that is **$412.40 to $1,184.60**. Your other EOBs from this year would pin it down.
messages.flag: A range where an input is missing — never a made-up exact number

messages.text: I met most of it in February. Here are my other EOBs from this year.
Got them. Your Feb 3 and Feb 20 EOBs put you at **$1,750.00** of your **$2,000.00** deductible before this scan. So only **$250.00** belongs on this one — not $965.25.

chip.text: source: your Feb 3 and Feb 20 EOBs

messages.flag: Remembers your case — every number traces to a document you can open

messages.text: After the deductible, your plan pays 80% of imaging and you pay 20%. 20% of the remaining **$1,812.00** is **$362.40**.
messages.spot: your plan pays 80% of imaging and you pay 20%

vars.finding_source: your Summary of Benefits — Imaging, 20% after deductible

chip.text: source: your Summary of Benefits — Imaging, 20% after deductible

messages.flag: Cites the plan clause it stands on — so you can check it

messages.text:
Billed: **$2,347.18**
Your insurer says you owe: **$1,184.60**
**What you should actually owe: $612.40**
messages.flag: Three numbers: the bill, the insurer's claim, and its own independent math

messages.text: Will I win if I dispute it?

I won't promise you'll win — nobody honest can, and I won't guess with your money. I also won't quote odds I don't have: there isn't yet an honest number for cases exactly like yours, and I'd rather tell you that than invent one. What I can tell you: your case rests on **your insurer's own EOBs**, and the best next step is **a call to member services asking them to re-run the claim with your deductible credited — I'll give you the script**.
